rows.grounds: fused form of yena (relative pronoun) and eva (emphatic particle); analyzed as given
compound of kṛta (done) and mātra (mere), expressing sufficiency of the act alone
being or spirit that acts as the seizing agent
denotes the act of taking possession of a person
the human being who is seized

items.question: By what mere act can a spirit seize a human being?
premises: A particular act is identified as the operative cause.
The mere performance of that act is sufficient.
Upon that mere performance a spirit seizes a human.
items.inference: Therefore the specified mere act enables a spirit to seize a human being.
uncertainties: The specific act referred to by yenaiva depends on the preceding context.
items.plain_english: By the mere doing of which, a spirit seizes a human being.
